title: RAG workflow overview
text: A retrieval-augmented generation system first retrieves relevant document chunks and then provides those chunks to a language model. Separating retrieval from generation makes sources traceable and allows the knowledge collection to be updated without retraining the generator.

title: Hybrid search with Elasticsearch
text: Hybrid retrieval combines sparse BM25 search with dense vector search. BM25 is effective for exact terms, identifiers, and names. Dense vectors help recover semantically related passages even when the query uses different words. Reciprocal rank fusion combines the two ranked result lists without comparing their incompatible raw scores.

title: Coarse and fine ranking
text: The coarse ranking stage uses reciprocal rank fusion to reduce the combined BM25 and dense candidates to roughly twenty to fifty chunks. A cross-encoder or generative reranker then scores each query and chunk pair for fine ranking. The best three to five chunks become context for answer generation.

title: Ascend model execution
text: Embedding and reranking models run in the NPU application container with torch_npu and device npu. Elasticsearch is a separate CPU-only container. The host-network NPU container reaches the Elasticsearch HTTP endpoint through localhost while model files and index data remain on RAID storage.

title: Grounded answer generation
text: After fine ranking, the application builds a prompt from the selected chunks and their source identifiers. The generation model must answer from that context and return citations. If retrieval finds no relevant evidence, the application should report insufficient evidence instead of inventing a source.
